headline: Lowest pay raised by record 142% in new National Pay Scale 2026
summary: Government employees will receive arrears from July 1, with basic salary adjustments unfolding in phases through 2027.
details: The Ministry of Finance has issued a gazette notification implementing the National Pay Scale 2026 retrospectively from July 1. This marks the largest pay hike for the civil service since independence, with the lowest pay increasing by a record 142 percent and top officials' basic salaries doubling.
Government employees will receive arrears for the period between July 1 and the date the official order was issued. Basic salary adjustments will be implemented in phases based on employee grades.

For employees in Grades 10 to 20, 50 percent of the total basic salary increase will be added from July 1 to December 31, 2026. This will rise to 75 percent from January 1 to June 30, 2027, reaching 100 percent by July 1, 2027.

For officials in Grades 1 to 9, 40 percent of the total basic salary increase will be disbursed from July 1 to December 31, 2026. This will increase to 70 percent from January 1, 2027, and reach full adjustment by July 1, 2027.
All other allowances will continue at existing rates until December 31, 2027, with revised allowance rates taking effect on January 1, 2028.
The previous national pay scale introduced in 2015 had seen basic pay rise by 95 percent in the top grade and 101 percent in the lowest grade.

For employees in Grades 10 to 20, 50 percent of the total basic salary increase will be added from July 1 to December 31, 2026. This will rise to 75 percent from January 1 to June 30, 2027, reaching 100 percent by July 1, 2027.

headline: 1,053 dead as measles outbreak kills 5 children in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a surge in measles cases, with over 1,000 deaths since April.
details: Five children died from measles and related symptoms across Bangladesh in just 24 hours, according to the DGHS control room.
A total of 1,20 new patients were identified during this period, as reported in a press release on Saturday.
The deaths included one confirmed case of measles and four suspected cases.
Since April 10, the total number of deaths related to measles has reached 1,053.
The health authorities continue to monitor the situation as the outbreak persists across the country.
